newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 23.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

* The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 33.87 points at 6,850.03 on Wednesday, and virtually all of the loss stemmed from IBM, which tumbled $10.375 to $157.625. The drop in the index snapped a four-session string of record closes.

* Indonesia will raise the minimum wage by an average 10.07 percent effective April 1, Manpower Minister Abdul Latief said on Wednesday. Indonesia in April 1996 raised the minimum wage by an average 10.63 percent.
* The Jakarta composite index closed up 5.24 points, or 0.77 percent, on Wednesday at 686.12 points after peaking at 687.65. The previous record of 681.94 points was achieved on April 4, 1990.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,372.25/72.75 in early trading against the opening of 2,371.25/71.75.
* Bank BNI on market talk of a possible better-than-expected 1996 net profit.
* Telkom on reports it was studying the possibility of launching a cable television network.
* Transportation firm Centris on market talk that the firm was likely to require another transportation firm.
* Tapioca starch maker Budi Acid on reports it was in negotiation to set up two joint ventures with local and Japanese firms.
* State-controlled tin miner Tambang Timah on news reports it has submitted a proposal to have a stake in the huge Busang gold find in Kalimantan.
* Bakrie Brothers on reports it was in negotiation to sell its 49-percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama which has a 9.36-percent stake in PT Freeport Indonesia.
* Semen Gresik on reports that it will hold a tender to operate its 50-megawatt power plant to supply electricity to its Tonasa-IV plant in south Sulawesi following technical problems.
